I have farmed this land for 48 years. I never went to school. My mother-in-law showed me how to do things when I first came to this village as a young bride, and since then I watch what my neighbors do and I copy what works. I keep everything in my head. My oldest son helps me carry the fertilizer bags now because my back is not as strong as it was.

I have 8 mu. I do it like this: 5 mu for wheat and then maize on that same ground, 2 mu for cotton, and 1 mu for mungbean along the east edge.

---

**Wheat and Maize** — these are my main crops. The wheat goes in every October after the maize comes off. Before I plow, I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — that big red bag, 50 jin. Then in March when the wheat starts to turn green again and I see the stems starting to thicken, I put urea on top. Last year I used 30 jin per mu at that time. But my neighbor Old Wang on the south end uses 35 jin and her wheat is always a bit taller and heavier than mine at harvest. This year I will use 35 jin too. I water 4 times: once right before I sow to get moisture down, once in November for wintering, once at jointing in April, once when it flowers in May. I spray twice — once for rust and once for aphids. I get around 450–475 jin per mu most years. I hope to push it to 500 this year.

Right after wheat harvest in June I turn around and plant maize on the same ground. I do not plow deep — just the rotary machine that our village cooperative brings. For maize I use hybrid seed, everyone in our village uses Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335, so I do the same as my neighbors. I apply one bag of compound fertilizer before planting and then two big handfuls of urea per mu when the maize is about knee-high and again at tasseling. I water twice — once when it is young if there is no rain, and once when the ears are filling. I spray for corn borer — maybe twice. I usually get 500–600 jin per mu.

**Cotton** — My mother-in-law always grew cotton and I keep 2 mu of it. Cotton is a lot of work. I plant in late April after the last cold snap. I use the improved seed from the seed shop in town — I do not save my own cotton seed anymore because the dealer says the improved ones resist bollworm better, and I believe him because my cotton did get hit hard about six years ago before I switched. Cotton needs a lot of fertilizer and a lot of spraying. I put compound fertilizer before planting, then I add urea and potash twice during the season — once when it starts to branch and once when the bolls are swelling. I water 4 times. I spray 7 times for bollworm, aphids, and spider mite — cotton always needs more spraying than anything else. I usually pick about 250–260 jin of seed cotton per mu.

**Mungbean** — I grow 1 mu of mungbean. It does not need much. I put a half-bag of compound fertilizer in before sowing and that is about it. Mungbean fixes its own, my mother-in-law always said that. I water twice. I spray once for bean beetles. I get about 120 jin per mu. We eat some and sell the rest at the village market.
